did.abstract: The Department of Photography and Imaging (DPI) is a four-year Bachelor of Fine Arts (BFA) program within the Tisch School of the Arts at New York University (NYU). The department focuses on both the creation and analysis of visual media, while also combining a studio art curriculum with a foundation in the liberal arts. The Records of the Tisch School of the Arts, Department of Photography and Imaging (dated 1982-2019) consists of materials created and collected by the DPI. The majority of the collection includes analog audio and video recordings of the department's events, guest lectures, and panel sessions. Other materials include catalogs of student works; programs and photographs from exhibitions; photographs from events; and magazines, including copies of ISO magazine.
did.physloc: Materials are stored offsite and advance notice is required for use. Please request materials at least two business days prior to your research visit to coordinate access.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: The Records of the Tisch School of the Arts, Department of Photography and Imaging (dated 1982-2019) consists of materials created and collected by the DPI at the NYU Tisch School of the Arts. The majority of the collection consists of analog audio and video recordings of the department's events, guest lectures, and panel sessions. Other materials include BFA catalogs that highlight the photographic works of students; programs and photographs from exhibitions of student works; photographs from events and programs affiliated with the DPI; and magazines, including copies of ISO magazine – Tisch's photography and literary magazine.

bioghist.head: Historical Note
bioghist.p: The Department of Photography and Imaging (DPI) is a four-year Bachelor of Fine Arts (BFA) program within the Tisch School of the Arts at New York University (NYU). The department focuses on both the creation and analysis of visual media, while also combining a studio art curriculum with a foundation in the liberal arts. The DPI supports a range of photographic methodologies; student and faculty work across analog and digital photo-based processes; as well as multimedia, new media, and post-photographic 3D simulation technologies.

acqinfo.head: Immediate Source of Acquisition
acqinfo.p: Transferred by Tisch School of the Arts Department of Photography and Imaging in September 2017. The accession number associated with this transfer is 2019.037. Accretions were transferred in November 2019. The accession numbers associated with these transfers are 2019.120 and 2019.121.

prefercite.head: Preferred Citation
prefercite.p: Identification of item, date; Tisch School of the Arts Department of Photography and Imaging Publications; RG 35.5; box number; folder number or item identifier; New York University Archives, New York University.

processinfo.head: Processing Information
processinfo.p: At the time of accessioning, materials were rehoused into archival boxes and folders. Materials were described on the collection-level with a box-list inventory. Born-digital items were identified and inventoried, but not forensically imaged, analyzed, or described at this time.

In spring 2025, students from NYU's Moving Image Archiving and Preservation (MIAP) program prepared an item-level inventory of the non-commercial audiovisual recordings housed within the collection. At this time, students identified one moldy VHS tape, which was separated from the collection and treated by NYU's Barbara Goldsmith Preservation and Conservation Department. This item is currently isolated from other items by housing them in a polyethylene bag with a desiccated board and RH monitor strip. If this strip indicates an RH greater than 50%, the Preservation Department should be contacted ASAP. Do not open this packaging without contacting the Preservation Department.

In summer 2026, this collection was arranged and described by an archivist. Paper materials, which were already housed in archival-quality folders and boxes, remained in their current folders and boxes. Original folder titles were retained whenever possible, but new titles were assigned as needed. Oversized materials were rehoused into appropriately sized folders and boxes.

Analog audiovisual media including VHS tapes, Betamax tapes, and a U-Matic tape remained in their original archival housing. Smaller analog audiovisual media including audiocassette tapes, Hi8 tapes, and miniDV tapes were rehoused into appropriately sized boxes. Each analog audiovisual item was assigned an individual identifying number and while related materials were physically separated by format, they were intellectually integrated together in the finding aid. Original titles were retained whenever possible, but new titles were assigned as needed.

New York University Libraries follows professional standards and best practices when imaging, ingesting, and processing born-digital material in order to maintain the integrity of the content. While the initial inventory listed 175 born-digital items, physical verification located only 98, likely due to duplicate entries in the original log. Out of the 98 born-digital items, 30 optical discs were forensically imaged, analyzed, and arranged using Forensics Toolkit (see appraisal note for more details). The electronic records were intellectually incorporated into the finding aid.

phystech.head: Audiovisual Access Policies and Procedures
phystech.p: Audiovisual materials have not been preserved and may not be available to researchers. Materials not yet digitized will need to have access copies made before they can be used. To request an access copy, or if you are unsure if an item has been digitized, please contact University Archives, special.collections@nyu.edu, 212-998-2596 with the collection name, collection number, and a description of the item(s) requested. A staff member will respond to you with further information.

phystech.head: Born-Digital Access Policies and Procedures.
phystech.p: An access terminal for born-digital materials in the collection is available by appointment for reading room viewing and listening only. Researchers may view an item's original container and/or carrier, but the physical carriers themselves are not available for use because of preservation concerns.

appraisal.head: Appraisal
appraisal.p: During the course of processing in summer 2026, the following copyrighted materials were removed from the collection: 22 VHS tapes, 3 audiocassette tapes, 34 optical discs, and 41 DVDs. 8 optical discs were removed from the collection because they were blank, contained duplicate materials, or unsupported file types.

arrangement.head: Arrangement
arrangement.p: Materials in this series are arranged in alphabetical order by topic. For topics with multiple audiovisual items, formats, and/or dates, materials are further arranged in chronological order.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: The majority of the collection can be found in Series I, which includes analog audio and video recordings of the department's events, guest lectures, and panel sessions. Guest lecturers include, but are not limited to: Bruce Gilden, Walter Rosenblum, Lee Witkins, Allan Sekula, Clarissa Sligh, Fred Ritchin, Lauri Novak, M.M. Sera, Ruth Orkin, and Stephen Apicela-Hitchcock.

The series also includes digital photographs that document student exhibitions; events related to Deborah Willis, Ph.D., the University Professor and Chair of the DPI at the Tisch School of the Arts at New York University, as of 2026; and the Tisch Summer High School Residency Program, an intensive four-week pre-college program open to high school sophomores and juniors.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: This series documents the photographic and literary works of Tisch students studying within the Department of Photography and Imaging. This series includes BFA catalogs that highlight the photographic works of students; programs and photographs from exhibitions of student works; photographs used in publications; and magazines, including copies of ISO magazine, Tisch's photography and literary magazine.
